questions.question:
Which following statement is true?
a) All graphs are trees
b) All trees are graphs
c) Some trees are graphs
d) No tree is a graph
questions.explanation: Every tree is a connected acyclic graph, so it is a special case of a graph, but graphs may contain cycles or be disconnected. Hence all trees are graphs, not the reverse.

questions.question:
Which of the following is false in the case of a spanning tree of a graph G?
a) It is a tree that spans G
b) It is a sub-graph of G
c) It includes every vertex of G
d) It can be either cyclic or acyclic

options.A: It is a tree that spans G
options.B: It is a sub-graph of G
options.C: It includes every vertex of G
options.D: It can be either cyclic or acyclic

questions.explanation: A spanning tree must be connected, acyclic and include every vertex, so it can never contain a cycle. That makes statement D false.

questions.question:
MST full form is:
a) Maximum Spanning Tree
b) Maximum Sub Tree
c) Minimum Spanning Tree
d) Minimum Sub Tree
questions.explanation: MST stands for Minimum Spanning Tree, the spanning tree with the smallest total edge weight. A maximum spanning tree is a different problem.

questions.question:
Topological sort can be applied to which of the following graphs?
a) Undirected Cyclic Graphs
b) Directed Cyclic Graphs
c) Undirected Acyclic Graphs
d) Directed Acyclic Graphs
questions.explanation: A topological order must respect every directed edge, which becomes impossible once a directed cycle exists, so it applies only to directed acyclic graphs (DAGs).

questions.question:
A circuit that does not repeat vertices is called ________.
a) cycle
b) path
c) tree
d) directed graph
questions.explanation: A cycle is a closed walk that returns to its starting vertex without repeating intermediate ones. A path is open and does not close on itself.

questions.question:
What type of approach does Prim's algorithm use to find a minimum spanning tree of a graph?
a. Divide and Conquer
b. Dynamic Programming
c. Greedy Approach
d. Backtracking
questions.explanation: Prim's algorithm is greedy: it repeatedly adds the cheapest edge that connects a new vertex to the tree grown so far. It uses neither DP nor backtracking.

questions.question:
Which of the following is true?
a) Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex
b) Prim's algorithm initializes with an edge
c) Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex which has smallest edge
d) Prim's algorithm initializes with a forest

options.A: Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex
options.B: Prim's algorithm initializes with an edge
options.C: Prim's algorithm initializes with a vertex which has smallest edge
options.D: Prim's algorithm initializes with a forest

questions.explanation: Prim's algorithm may begin at any vertex and grows one tree from it, choosing edges only afterwards. Kruskal's instead starts from the global edge list.

questions.question:
What is the time complexity of Kruskal's algorithm (E is the number of edges and V is the number of vertices of input graph)?
a) O(log V)
b) O(E log V)
c) O(E²)
d) O(V log E)
questions.explanation: Kruskal's sorts the E edges, costing O(E log E), and each union-find check is nearly constant, so the total is O(E log V) since E ≤ V².

questions.question:
Which of the following algorithms is used to find the shortest path in a graph with negative edge weights?
a. Dijkstra's Algorithm
b. Prim's Algorithm
c. Bellman-Ford Algorithm
d. Kruskal's Algorithm
questions.explanation: Bellman-Ford relaxes all edges repeatedly, which tolerates negative weights and even reports a negative cycle. Dijkstra's algorithm fails in that situation.

questions.question:
Dijkstra's algorithm is used for finding ________.
a) minimum spanning tree
b) shortest path
c) string matching
d) sorted sequence
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the least-cost route from one source to every other vertex in a weighted graph. MST algorithms solve a different problem.

questions.question:
Dijkstra's algorithm is known as:
a) All pair shortest path
b) All pair longest path
c) Single Source longest Path
d) Single Source shortest path
questions.explanation: It is a single-source shortest-path algorithm: distances from one chosen source to all vertices. All-pairs versions are Floyd-Warshall or repeated Dijkstra.

questions.question:
Which of the following algorithms are used to find the shortest path from a source node to all other nodes in a weighted graph?
a) BFS
b) Dijkstra's Algorithm
c) Prim's Algorithm
d) Kruskal's Algorithm
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm handles weighted graphs, while BFS works only when every edge costs the same. Prim and Kruskal build spanning trees, not shortest paths.

questions.question:
Floyd Warshall Algorithm used to solve the shortest path problem has a time complexity of:
a) O(VV)
b) O(VVV)
c) O(EV)
d) O(E*E)
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall runs three nested loops over the vertices, so its time is O(V³) and its space O(V²). That is why the printed option reads VVV.

questions.question:
What is the worst case time complexity of Prim's algorithm if adjacency matrix is used?
a) O(log V)
b) O(V²)
c) O(E²)
d) O(V log E)
questions.explanation: With an adjacency matrix, finding the minimum-distance unvisited vertex needs a scan of V per step, giving O(V²) in total. Adjacency lists with a heap improve this.

questions.question:
A graph is called a ________ if it is a connected acyclic graph.
a) cyclic graph
b) regular graph
c) tree
d) forest
questions.explanation: A connected acyclic graph is a tree, with n-1 edges for n vertices. A forest is acyclic as well, but it need not be connected.

questions.question:
What is the number of edges in a tree with n nodes?
a) n
b) n-1
c) n+1
d) 2n-1
questions.explanation: A tree with n vertices has exactly n-1 edges: n-1 edges connect them all, and any extra edge would close a cycle.

questions.question:
DAG full form is:
a) Direct Aligned Graph
b) Direct Acyclic Graph
c) Defined Aligned Graph
d) Defined Acyclic Graph
questions.explanation: DAG means Directed Acyclic Graph — a directed graph with no directed cycle, used for dependency and scheduling orders.

questions.question:
What is sink in a graph?
a) A vertex with no incoming edges
b) A vertex with no outgoing edges
c) A vertex with highest degree
d) A vertex connecting two components

options.A: A vertex with no incoming edges
options.B: A vertex with no outgoing edges

questions.explanation: A sink has out-degree zero, so no edge leaves it and every path ends there. A source, by contrast, has in-degree zero.

questions.question:
Define in-degree of a graph.
a) Number of edges going out of a vertex
b) Number of edges coming into a vertex
c) Total number of edges in a graph
d) Number of vertices adjacent to a vertex

options.A: Number of edges going out of a vertex
options.B: Number of edges coming into a vertex
options.C: Total number of edges in a graph
options.D: Number of vertices adjacent to a vertex

questions.explanation: In-degree counts the directed edges that arrive at a vertex, while out-degree counts those that leave. In an undirected graph the two combine into the degree.

questions.question:
What is cut vertex?
a) A vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components
b) A vertex with maximum degree
c) A vertex with minimum degree
d) A vertex with no adjacent vertices

options.A: A vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components
options.D: A vertex with no adjacent vertices

questions.explanation: A cut vertex, or articulation point, is one whose removal increases the number of connected components. Such vertices mark weak points in a network.

questions.question:
Write one difference between path and cycle.
a) A path starts and ends at the same vertex; a cycle does not
b) A cycle starts and ends at the same vertex; a path does not
c) Both path and cycle start and end at the same vertex
d) Neither path nor cycle can repeat vertices

options.A: A path starts and ends at the same vertex; a cycle does not
options.B: A cycle starts and ends at the same vertex; a path does not
options.C: Both path and cycle start and end at the same vertex
options.D: Neither path nor cycle can repeat vertices

questions.explanation: A cycle begins and ends at the same vertex, which a path does not. Both may avoid repeating intermediate vertices.

Which algorithm is commonly used as the basis for Topological Sorting?
a) BFS only
b) DFS only
c) Both BFS and DFS can be used
d) Dijkstra's algorithm

options.C: Both BFS and DFS can be used

questions.explanation: Kahn's algorithm uses BFS with in-degree counts, while the DFS method emits vertices in reverse finish order, so both approaches work.

questions.question:
Floyd-Warshall algorithm is based on which algorithm design paradigm?
a) Greedy Method
b) Divide and Conquer
c) Dynamic Programming
d) Backtracking
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall improves the estimate for each pair by trying every vertex as an intermediate hop, which is bottom-up dynamic programming.

questions.question:
In a directed graph, each edge has:
a) No direction
b) A direction from one vertex to another
c) Two directions simultaneously
d) Direction only if it is a cycle

options.B: A direction from one vertex to another
options.D: Direction only if it is a cycle

questions.explanation: In a digraph each edge is an ordered pair, drawn as an arrow from source to destination. Undirected edges have no orientation at all.

questions.question:
What does Bellman-Ford algorithm do when a negative weight cycle is detected?
a) Ignores the cycle and continues
b) Reports that no shortest path exists
c) Converts negative edges to positive
d) Applies Dijkstra's algorithm instead

options.B: Reports that no shortest path exists

questions.explanation: A negative cycle lets the path cost fall without limit, so no shortest path exists and Bellman-Ford reports that after V-1 relaxation rounds.

a) Stack
b) Queue
c) Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
d) Priority Queue
questions.explanation: Kruskal's uses a disjoint-set (union-find) structure to test whether two endpoints are already connected, which makes cycle detection almost constant time.

questions.question:
Why does Dijkstra's algorithm fail on graphs with negative edge weights?
a) It cannot process weighted graphs
b) It assumes all edge weights are non-negative for the greedy choice to be correct
c) It runs in infinite loops
d) It only works on undirected graphs

options.B: It assumes all edge weights are non-negative for the greedy choice to be correct
options.D: It only works on undirected graphs

questions.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm finalises a vertex once its distance is the smallest, assuming no later path can be cheaper — an assumption that negative edges break.

A forest in graph theory is defined as:
a) A connected graph with cycles
b) A disconnected acyclic graph
c) A directed graph with no vertices
d) A graph where every vertex has degree 2

options.C: A directed graph with no vertices
options.D: A graph where every vertex has degree 2

questions.explanation: A forest is an acyclic graph that may be disconnected, so it is a collection of trees. A single connected acyclic graph is one tree.
